I am thinking about this year on my 10.1 mu. My wife and I are getting older, and our son works in the city, sends some money but is not here for the busy days. I have been doing wheat-maize rotation here for 35 years, same as everyone in our village.

For wheat, I planted last October already — improved variety from the agro-station, Jimai I think they call it. I bought 2 bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before sowing, that is 50 kg, plus I will topdress urea at jointing in March, about one bag (50 kg) for every 2 mu, so around 25 kg urea per mu. The urea is mostly nitrogen. I will water from the well — once before winter, once at jointing, once at heading. Three waterings is enough if rain comes. I spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around April, sometimes twice if I see the leaves turning. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, the year before 480, so I expect similar.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I do no-till — too tired to plough, and the neighbors all do this now with the seeder. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has. I put one bag of compound fertilizer at sowing (50 kg/mu, 15-15-15) and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 30 kg per mu. Maize needs more nitrogen than wheat. I water once or twice depending on rain — usually once at tasseling. Spray once for borers. Maize gives me about 550 kg per mu in a good year.

I do not change much from year to year. What works, works. Fertilizer prices went up but I cannot risk cutting back — losing yield costs more than the extra fertilizer.
